questions.prompt: A 12-stage task has p=0.97 per stage. End-to-end success? (3 decimals)
Per-stage success required for 90% over 20 equal stages? (4 decimals)
The weakest stage of a 5-stage chain has p=0.6, the others 0.98. Which change most improves end-to-end success?
options: Raising the weakest stage from 0.6 to 0.8.
Raising each strong stage from 0.98 to 0.99.
Collecting more data for the strongest stage.
questions.explanation: Product: weakest factor dominates (0.6->0.8 multiplies by 1.33).

questions.prompt: Episode log, 3 stages: [T,T,T], [T,F], [T,T,F], [T,T,T], [F]. Conditional success rate of stage 2? (3 decimals)

A 3-stage task is run for 5 episodes; each list shows the stage results actually attempted (an episode stops at its first failure): [T,T,T], [T,F], [T,T,F], [T,T,T], [F]. What is the end-to-end success rate? (2 decimals)
p=0.9, d=0.5, R=2: probability of true success on a stage? (4 decimals)
One stage has success probability p=0.9 per attempt, failure detection probability d=0.5 and at most R=2 attempts. What is the probability of a silent failure (an undetected failure)? (4 decimals)
Once R>=2, which usually raises end-to-end task success more: increasing detection d or increasing R?
options: Increasing d, because silent failures are never retried and are the dominant loss.
Neither affects true success, since the outcome is fixed by the first attempt.
They are equivalent, since both raise the number of successful attempts equally.
Increasing R, because retries are free and rescue every failed attempt.
questions.explanation: Silent failures are never retried; extra attempts add little.

questions.prompt: Skill B works only if the object is within 2 cm of nominal. Skill A leaves a position error with SD 1 cm (normal). Roughly what fraction of chains start B in its working range?
A planner combines a language model's skill probability with a success probability by multiplication. What does this prevent?
options: Any hallucination by the language model, since low scores are removed.
Choosing a plausible step that the robot can rarely execute successfully.
The compounding of errors over a long sequence of executed steps.
Choosing a step that the language model itself finds very unlikely.
questions.explanation: Affordance multiplies the LM score down for infeasible skills.

questions.prompt: LM scores (0.4,0.4,0.2), success probabilities (0.9,0.3,0.8). Highest product score? (2 decimals)
